newsitem.title: USA: No budget deal yet, talks to resume - U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: No budget deal yet, talks to resume - U.S. official.

text.p: Negotiators for President Clinton and congressional Republicans have not yet reached a balanced budget agreement, and the two sides are to resume talks later Friday, an administration official said.
"As of right now there are still a small number of issues that are unresolved. We're not there yet," said the official.
White House officials are expected to go to Capitol Hill to resume talks later today, the official said.
The official declined comment on the chances of a deal being reached and said the administration had made plans for all possible outcomes to the talks, including their failure.
"We have contingency planning for any possibility ... including no deal," said the official.
Another administration official said early today that the main sticking point in the talks, which aim to hammer out an accord to balance the budget by the year 2002, remained taxes.
"This is a really difficult problem -- taxes," said the official.
Both administration officials asked not to be identified.
